name: Melktert
summary: Milk tart: a crisp sweet pastry shell filled with smooth, cinnamon-scented milk custard and dusted with cinnamon.
about: Melktert came to the Cape with Dutch settlers in the 1600s and has been reworked by every generation since; C. Louis Leipoldt noted that almost every cook had their own way of making it. A cinnamon-dusted slice is the bake-sale, church-tea and Sunday-afternoon classic, and 27 February is National Milk Tart Day.
steps: Beat the butter and castor sugar together until pale and creamy, 2–3 minutes, then beat in the egg.
Sift in the flour, baking powder and salt and mix to a soft dough. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C if your oven is a fan oven). Press the dough into a 23 cm pie dish, about 4 mm thick, up the sides too. Prick the base with a fork, line with baking paper and fill with dried beans or rice.
Bake for 15 minutes, lift out the paper and beans and bake for 10–12 minutes more, until pale golden and dry. Leave to cool.
For the filling, heat the milk, cinnamon stick and butter in a saucepan over medium heat until small bubbles form at the edge, 5–7 minutes. Remove the cinnamon stick.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, flour, cornflour and vanilla to a smooth paste. Whisk in a cup of the hot milk, then pour it all back into the saucepan.
Cook over medium-low heat, whisking all the time, for 5–7 minutes, until it thickens like custard and bubbles. Keep whisking for 1 minute more so it loses any floury taste.

Pour the hot filling into the pastry shell, smooth the top and dust generously with ground cinnamon. Cool for 30 minutes, then refrigerate for at least 3 hours, until set firm enough to slice cleanly.
prepNote: Make it the day before and keep it chilled; dust with fresh cinnamon before serving.
